[RDSC.4a.9.6] **A bind index names a slot of its site's frame, and one outside
it faults where it is used.** `Expr.bind_ref` and `BindExpr.bind_index`
(`proto/rete_expr.proto#Expr`, `proto/rete_expr.proto#BindExpr`) name a slot of the
bind frame of the site that holds them ([IRET.9.4]): a terminal's frame has
`bind_count` slots ([RLOW.4.5.3.1]), a slot's conversion has one ([RDSC.5.5.9]),
and a node's test has none ([IRET.9.2]). Each field is `uint32` on the wire and
reserves no value, so every index is one its field can hold, and a loader
**must not** refuse an artefact for an index outside its frame.

Wherever the engine reads or writes an index outside its site's frame, it
**must** raise an `EngineError` (`proto/engine_fault.proto#EngineFault`) whose
fault is `ENGINE_FAULT_ARTEFACT_LIED`, naming the node or rule that used it
([LERR.9.11]), and halt the tier ([LERR.1.4.7]). It **must not** read a value, skip
the write or answer `null`. In a host's conversion the fault is one the conversion
meets, and the call answers as [NFCT.1.4.6] states.

An index inside its frame that is read before the `bind` writing it has run is
[RARC.5.6.11]'s, and is no `ARTEFACT_LIED`.
